principle: Microcopy / grammatical correctness · Refactoring UI — copy that reads like a human wrote it
location: PLANNER → STREAK widget, microcopy below the day count (PlannerStreakCell.tsx)
screenshot: ss_67940ojql (right panel, 'STREAK / 1 DAYS / 1 days - don't break the chain.')
problem: After my first day of activity, the streak widget shows `1 DAYS` in the headline number and the supporting copy reads `1 days - don't break the chain.` — both use the plural `days` for a single-day streak. It's the kind of small grammar slip a painter will read once and trust the rest of the app a little less. Same widget will read correctly at 2+.
fix: Pluralise based on count: `count === 1 ? 'DAY' : 'DAYS'` in the headline label, and `count === 1 ? '1 day — don't break the chain.' : count + ' days — don't break the chain.'` in the supporting line. Replace the ASCII hyphen with an em-dash to match the rest of the app's punctuation style.

principle: Project Button discipline (P13.1) · CLAUDE memory ('no cyan on action buttons; cyan reserved for status dots/links')
location: ManageInspoModal.tsx → `SAVE ORDER` button in the header of the Manage Inspo modal
screenshot: ss_9115i4nuw (modal header, solid cyan/blue 'SAVE ORDER' button next to ghost 'CLOSE')
problem: The `SAVE ORDER` button in the inspo manage modal is rendered as solid cyan/light-blue. The project's stated Button discipline forbids cyan on action buttons (cyan = status indicator, links, accent). Other primary actions across the app use green for create/save (ADD EVENT, ADD INSPO, NEW PROJECT, ADD UNIT all solid green) — so this button breaks the pattern recruits have already learned.
fix: Switch `SAVE ORDER` to `variant="success"` so it matches the green save/create idiom used by ADD EVENT, ADD INSPO, NEW PROJECT. One-line change in `ManageInspoModal.tsx`.

principle: NN/g #1 Visibility of system status · NN/g #9 Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors
location: PlannerInspoCell.tsx / InspoGalleryGrid.tsx — `` rendering when external host returns non-200 or refuses hotlink
screenshot: ss_2484ewa93 + ss_2228gukku (broken images render as just the alt-text on a transparent panel with no visible frame or error state)
problem: Both my test inspo images (pinimg + unsplash) returned `503` to the browser in this audit environment — the `` simply ends up with `naturalWidth: 0` and renders only the alt text floating in the gallery cell with no border, broken-image glyph, or error label. The widget already validates URL shape on submit but does not check that the image actually loads or surface a fallback when it doesn't. A painter on flaky cafe WiFi or hitting Pinterest's hotlink-protection randomly will see their reference board look broken and won't know it's a transient failure vs. a permanent dead link.
fix: Add an `onError` handler on the `` that sets local state → renders a styled fallback tile: a `frame`-bordered grey box with a small image-broken Lucide icon and the muted-foreground copy `Couldn't load — open source`, where the alt text becomes the tile's hover title and the underlying URL is still clickable (opens in new tab). Add `referrerPolicy="no-referrer"` and `loading="lazy"` (already lazy) to the `` to maximise the odds of the load succeeding from Pinterest in the first place.

principle: NN/g #4 Consistency and standards · ISO 8601 month convention (humans expect 1=Jan ... 12=Dec in URLs)
location: /projects?calYear=YYYY&calMonth=MM URL param contract · CalendarMonthGrid.tsx + the page-level search-params reader
screenshot: ss_4890loyzg (calMonth=7 displays August 2026) + ss_2551ntyvc (calMonth=6 displays July 2026) + ss_5450wf6hj (calMonth=0 displays January 2026)
problem: The `calMonth` URL search param is 0-indexed (Jan=0, Jun=5, Jul=6, Aug=7, Dec=11) — matching JavaScript's `Date.getMonth()` internal convention but contradicting the universal human convention that `month 7` means July. Anyone who bookmarks a calendar view, shares a URL to teammates, or hand-edits the URL to nav forward a month will land on the wrong month. The component doc-comment on line 51 of CalendarMonthGrid.tsx even concedes `0-based month index (Jan = 0)` — i.e. this is a deliberate choice but it's a UX trap. Out-of-range values (calMonth=15) correctly fall back to current month, which is good — just the 0-indexing itself is the wart.
fix: Parse `calMonth` as 1-indexed at the URL boundary (the page-level Server Component that reads the search params), subtract 1 only when handing to the grid component. Update the grid's `navigate(delta)` URLSearchParams.set call to write `String(nextMonth + 1)`. Pure boundary fix: no internal logic changes, no migration of stored data. Comment in CalendarMonthGrid.tsx changes from `0-based month index` to `1-based month index in URL, 0-based internally`.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.3.1 Info and Relationships · screen-reader labels should be meaningful prose
location: CalendarMonthGrid.tsx line 289 — gridcell `aria-label` formatted as raw ISO key
screenshot: n/a — DOM inspection (each day button has aria-label like `2026-06-08 · 1 event(s)`)
problem: Calendar day buttons use `${cell.key}${hasEvents ? ' · N event(s)' : ''}` for their aria-label, where `cell.key` is the raw ISO date `YYYY-MM-DD`. A screen reader reading `"2026-06-08"` speaks it as either `two thousand twenty-six dash zero six dash zero eight` or `twenty twenty-six dash six dash eight` depending on engine — neither of which is what a painter expects. The `aria-current="date"` on today is correct and the `role="gridcell"` is fine; it's only the label string that's machine-coded.
fix: Format the aria-label as `${MONTH_NAMES[focusedMonth]} ${cell.day}, ${focusedYear}${hasEvents ? `, ${dayEvents.length} ${dayEvents.length === 1 ? 'event' : 'events'}` : ''}` — e.g. `"June 8, 2026, 1 event"`. Today gets the prefix `Today, ` so the label reads `"Today, June 1, 2026"`. One-block edit in CalendarMonthGrid.tsx around line 285–290.

principle: NN/g #4 Consistency and standards — touch devices have no hover
location: PlannerHeatmapCell.tsx footer copy — `Your last 90 days of painting. Hover a cell for the count.`
screenshot: ss_5450wf6hj (mobile 375px, the heatmap footer still reads 'Hover a cell for the count')
problem: The heatmap's helper text is hard-coded to `Hover a cell for the count.` even on mobile breakpoints, where there is no hover — recruits on iPhone (P14.8 mobile pass is the whole point of this section) will read it and wonder what they're meant to do. The cell `title` attribute does double as a click-fallback on touch, but the copy doesn't tell them that.
fix: Change the footer string to `Hover or tap a cell for the count.` (or split via `useIsTouch()`-style hook into hover-only vs. tap-only variants). One-line content fix in PlannerHeatmapCell.tsx.

principle: NN/g #4 Consistency and standards — domain vocabulary alignment
location: PlannerHeatmapCell.tsx — tooltip title format on each cell, e.g. `4 actions · Mon 1 Jun`
screenshot: n/a — JS read of the title attribute on the green Jun cell
problem: The heatmap cells label their count as `N actions`, but the rest of the dashboard speaks in `activity` (ACTIVITY widget, `activity_log` schema, `getActivityByDay`). Painters reading `4 actions` may not immediately connect that to the activity stream they just watched populate. Minor language drift, not a bug.
fix: Switch the tooltip to `${count} ${count === 1 ? 'activity' : 'activities'} · ${dayLabel}` to align with the rest of the dashboard's vocabulary. Or use the more painter-natural `4 bumps · Mon 1 Jun` if all entries are stage bumps. Trivial copy change.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced) / §2.5.8 (Minimum) · the 24×24 CSS minimum and the 44×44 mobile floor
location: ManageInspoModal.tsx — drag-grip handle (left edge of each row in the manage list)
screenshot: ss_9115i4nuw (the ⋮⋮ drag dots at x≈432 on each row, ~8px wide)
problem: The drag-reorder handle in the manage modal renders as a tight ~8×16 cluster of dots. WCAG 2.5.8 wants 24×24 CSS minimum for any interactive control, and Apple HIG / iOS prefers 44×44 for primary touch targets. On a phone-sized modal, a painter trying to reorder their reference board will fat-finger this routinely.
fix: Pad the drag handle to a 32×32 (desktop) / 44×44 (mobile-via-tap-target class) hit area while keeping the visual dot cluster the same size. Wrap the icon in a `tap-target` button and rely on the project's existing CSS that already enforces the 40px floor on `tap-target`.
